stimulus.source_note: Treaty of Paris, signed December 10, 1898, public domain (abridged); photograph: raising the American flag at the Government House, Honolulu, August 12, 1898, public domain.
stimulus.text: "Article I. Spain relinquishes all claim of sovereignty over and title to Cuba. Article II. Spain cedes to the United States the island of Porto Rico and other islands now under Spanish sovereignty in the West Indies, and the island of Guam in the Marianas or Ladrones. Article III. Spain cedes to the United States the archipelago known as the Philippine Islands. . . ." — Treaty of Paris, signed December 10, 1898 (abridged). Background from the books: the United States agreed to pay Spain $20 million for the Philippine Islands.

source: original; stimulus is a verbatim abridged excerpt from the Treaty of Paris, December 10, 1898, public domain, with a public-domain 1898 photograph
stem: The photograph shows the American flag being raised in Honolulu in August 1898. Taken with the treaty, the photograph best illustrates that

options.text: Hawaii was ceded by Spain in the treaty
options.misconception: Spain never owned Hawaii; the treaty cedes only Porto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines.

options.text: The Philippines were annexed before Hawaii
options.misconception: Hawaii's flag went up in August 1898, months before the treaty ceding the Philippines was signed in December.

options.text: America added Pacific territory in the same year it won the war
The war against Spain was fought mainly in Hawaii and the Pacific
options.misconception: No battle of the war was fought in Hawaii; the fighting was in Cuba and the Philippines.

rationales.A: Spain never owned Hawaii, so the treaty could not cede it. Hawaii was annexed by the United States itself.
rationales.B: The dates run the other way: Hawaii's flag rose in August 1898, and the treaty was signed in December.
rationales.C: Background from the books: Hawaii was annexed in 1898, against the backdrop of the war, and the treaty added the Philippines the same year.
rationales.D: The war was fought in Cuba and the Philippines. Hawaii saw a flag-raising, not a battle.
rationales.general:
1. Date the photograph. The flag rises in Honolulu in August 1898.
2. Date the treaty. It was signed in December 1898, ceding the Philippines.
3. Put the year together. In one year the United States added Hawaii and the Philippines across the Pacific.
Remember: when two sources share a year, line up their dates and ask what happened in that one year.
